product_from_film: Zatanna turns demonstrated software workflows into programmatic actions for AI agents and manages the integration infrastructure.
explains_well: The script and diagrams explain the legacy-system problem, the workflow-to-call sequence and the infrastructure responsibilities.
unclear: No specific workflow is demonstrated from user action through generated calls to a changed record, so the core mechanism remains abstract.
scenario: Three founders explain connecting AI agents to legacy software, discovering requests from a workflow and running the resulting actions.
product_clear_basis: The 40–49s workflow diagram and script explain discovering requests and generating the call sequence; the earlier introduction only states coordination with operational software.

categories.finding: Captions and cards preserve the main proposition silently, but no actual legacy-system action supplies a concrete result.
Panels are generally placed beside speakers, though trees and strong backlight compete with thin pale UI details in some views.
The film spends substantial time on infrastructure and team history; the core mechanism receives a brief abstract checklist.
The access problem is answered by a proposed workflow conversion and managed execution layer, not a complete demonstrated business action.
Outdoor founder presence and simplified diagrams suggest approachability and confidence; response is unmeasured.
The same brand mark, cream cards and legacy-system framing connect the sections, but no single record or task persists through the process.
Reliability, request volume, customer revenue and broad system support are film claims. The table and diagrams do not establish measured performance or actual generated-call behavior.
The explicit legacy-system categories and infrastructure responsibilities are more specific than the central-agent diagram alone.
Replace some founder history with a complete small workflow.
